name: 91-hidden-csvsum
prompt:
Package `csvsum` sums one column of a comma-separated stream. Its public API is one function:

    func Sum(r io.Reader, column int) (float64, error)

The specification, in full:

1. The input is lines of comma-separated fields. `column` is 0-based.
2. Spaces around a field are not part of it: " 3.5 " is the number 3.5.
3. A line that is empty or contains only whitespace is skipped. It is not an error.
4. An input with no lines at all returns 0 and a nil error, as does an input of nothing but blank lines.
5. A line with fewer than column+1 fields returns an error whose message contains "line N: short row", where N is the 1-based position of that line in the input, counting the blank lines that were skipped.
6. A field that does not parse as a float returns an error whose message contains "line N: bad number", with N numbered exactly as in rule 5.
7. On any error, Sum returns the error; the float it returns alongside it is not read by anyone.
8. Sum must never panic, whatever the input.

The current implementation is in sum.go and satisfies none of the edge cases above. The visible test in sum_test.go covers the ordinary path only. Fix sum.go so the whole specification holds. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` must pass.
